messages:
sara-k: Quick Q — we're about to enable a nightly job that prunes 'trace_index' entries older than 90d. It currently includes an optional customer_id column when debug is enabled. Do we need an explicit retention/deletion approval before we flip it? @security-team :thinking:

mike-l: are those customer_ids real customer identifiers or internal mapping ids? if real, that's def something to approve. otherwise probably fine.

sara-k: good q. It's a real customer_id column we currently populate on rare debug runs. Plan: redact customer_id from the prune target (set NULL) and only delete rows with service/timestamp. Want to be sure that meets policy.

jun-chen: if you can redact before deletion that's fine. policy: deletions touching PII need either a retention exception or a documented audit and a ticket. if you remove PII beforehand, ops can run the job. I'll ping @oliver for final sign-off.

oliver: TL;DR: redact first or get exception. checklist: 1) PR that removes/NULLs customer_id 2) job runbook + S3 key snapshot 3) brief audit log entry. Once PR includes those I'm fine with flip. Example SQL to include in PR:

```sql
UPDATE trace_index
SET customer_id = NULL
WHERE timestamp < now() - interval '90 days' AND customer_id IS NOT NULL;
```

Also link the retention-exception doc: https://confluence.company/retention/exceptions

sec-bot: Reminder: retention exceptions must be submitted if deletion touches customer identifiers. See policy: /policies/data-retention

sara-k: copying this into the PR description. Will push PR later today and add runbook + snapshot. If we redact first, no exception ticket needed. Will update when ready :thumbsup:
